correctness.rationale: The normal-bundle sequence gives \(c(T_X)=(1+H)^5/((1+aH)(1+bH))\); expansion yields \(p_1=(5-a^2-b^2)H^2\), and the Hirzebruch signature theorem gives \(\sigma=ab(5-a^2-b^2)/3\). At fixed \(S=a+b\) and gap \(g=b-a\), one obtains \(-3\sigma=(S^4-10S^2+10g^2-g^4)/8\). The allowed gaps have the parity of \(S\), so direct comparison of \(f(g)=10g^2-g^4\) proves the complete maximizing classification. Exact-integer replay over 9,799 bidegrees agrees with every case.

value.rationale: The signature is an intrinsic oriented topological invariant used in classification of complete intersections. Fixing \(a+b\) fixes the canonical-polarization exponent \(K_X\cong\mathcal O_X(S-5)\), giving a natural geography slice. The theorem gives a complete sharp classification on that slice and reveals a nontrivial near-balance phenomenon: exact balance is not extremal for even \(S\), while odd \(S\) has a rigid two-type tie. This is a structural family theorem rather than a finite numerical observation.
